claims.evidence: Origin cannot be determined from photos of boxes.
Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the Nikon D750 box and manuals.
The camera body is wrapped in bubble wrap and its physical condition is not visible.
Requires a video of the device powered on and functioning.
The witness report and Photo 0/1 identify the model as a D750 based on the packaging and manuals.

risks.risk: The bubble-wrapped items may not be the advertised camera or may be a different/cheaper model.
risks.proof: A photo of the camera body and lens unwrapped showing the model name and serial number.
risks.if_unproven: as empty boxes or non-functional parts.

risks.risk: High shutter count or sensor damage.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the last photo's EXIF data showing the shutter count and a clear photo of the sensor.
risks.if_unproven: as a body near the end of its mechanical life.

risks.risk: Lens fungus or internal glass damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front and rear lens elements against a light source.
risks.if_unproven: as a lens with significant optical defects.

risks.risk: Gimbal motor failure or calibration issues.
risks.proof: A video showing the Zhiyun gimbal stabilizing a camera through its full range of motion.

proof_requests: Photos of the camera body, lens, and gimbal completely unwrapped.
A photo of the camera's bottom plate showing the model and serial number.
A screenshot of the shutter count from a recent photo.
Clear photos of the lens glass (front and back).
A video showing all items powered on and working.
response.reason: The actual items are not visible as they are wrapped in bubble wrap, and the seller has provided conflicting information regarding the model (D750 vs D850).
